import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Kill mass from numbers still addable whose forced partners (via S) sit at the edge of 1..n: an expanding-frontier pressure measure, normalised."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.shape[0]
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    A = (np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    if S.size == 0 or k == 0 or A.size == 0:
        return out

    v = cand[:, None].astype(np.int64)      # (k,1)
    s = S[None, :].astype(np.int64)         # (1,m)
    edge = 6  # thickness of frontier band

    # For each candidate v and chosen s, the four forced third values t.
    # Weight each produced t by how close it lies to an end of 1..n (frontier),
    # since numbers near the boundary have fewer partner solutions available.
    def edge_weight(t):
        # distance of t from either endpoint, mapped to [0,1], 1 at the boundary
        d = np.minimum(t - 1, n - t).astype(np.float64)
        return np.clip(1.0 - d / edge, 0.0, 1.0)

    mass = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    tt = [
        (a * v + b * s, c),   # t = (a*v + b*s)/c
        (b * v + a * s, c),   # t = (b*v + a*s)/c
        (c * v - b * s, a),   # t = (c*v - b*s)/a
        (c * v - a * s, b),   # t = (c*v - a*s)/b
    ]
    for num, den in tt:
        ok = (num % den == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // den, 0)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
        tc = np.clip(t, 1, n)
        not_v = tc != v
        not_s = tc != s
        av = avail[tc - 1]
        hit = valid & not_v & not_s & av
        # weight frontier contributions
        w = edge_weight(tc.astype(np.float64))
        mass += (hit.astype(np.float64) * w).sum(axis=1)

    # normalise: rough expected edge-weighted kills ~ m * (edge/n) * 4 / something; use m-scaled tanh
    denom = float(S.size) * (2.0 * edge / max(n, 1))
    return np.tanh(mass / (denom + mass + 1e-9))

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """For each candidate, the median over chosen s of the fractional slack of the nearest solvable third value, aggregated as density of close-but-not-exact resonances (a continuous 'near miss' pressure)."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    if S.size == 0:
        return out
    v = cand[:, None].astype(float)
    s = S[None, :].astype(float)
    # For each pairing, compute the "distance to exactness" for the three key forms,
    # measured as distance of the numerator to a multiple of the divisor, normalized.
    acc = np.zeros((k,), dtype=float)
    cnt = np.zeros((k,), dtype=float)

    def add(num, den):
        r = np.abs(num - den * np.round(num / den)) / den  # in [0, 0.5]
        # near-miss score: 1 - 2r in [0,1], high when close
        near = 1.0 - 2.0 * r
        # weight by how strong the resonance would be (1/(1+dist))
        acc_ = near / (1.0 + np.abs(num / den))
        return acc_, near

    # form1: z = (a*v + b*s)/c
    num1 = a * v + b * s
    n1, nr1 = add(num1, c)
    acc += nr1.sum(axis=1)
    cnt += S.size

    # form2: z = (a*s + b*v)/c
    num2 = a * s + b * v
    n2, nr2 = add(num2, c)
    acc += nr2.sum(axis=1)
    cnt += S.size

    # form3: y = (c*s - a*v)/b
    num3 = c * s - a * v
    n3, nr3 = add(num3, b)
    acc += nr3.sum(axis=1)
    cnt += S.size

    # form4: x = (c*s - b*v)/a
    num4 = c * s - b * v
    n4, nr4 = add(num4, a)
    acc += nr4.sum(axis=1)
    cnt += S.size

    return np.clip(acc / np.maximum(cnt, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Bounded signed ratio (K-C)/(K+C+1) of live-kill count K vs live-creation count C per candidate."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    V = np.arange(1, n + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    S = V[chosen]

    avail_pad = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=bool)
    avail_pad[1:] = avail

    # --- K[v]: number of distinct still-available w != v such that w, v, some s in S form a solution ---
    K = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    if S.size > 0:
        pair = np.zeros((n + 1, n + 1), dtype=bool)
        for s in S:
            s = int(s)
            for (num_fn, den) in (
                (c * V - a * s, b),
                (c * V - b * s, a),
                (c * s - a * V, b),
                (c * s - b * V, a),
                (a * V + b * s, c),
                (a * s + b * V, c),
            ):
                ok = (num_fn % den == 0)
                t = np.where(ok, num_fn // den, -1)
                good = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != V) & (t != s)
                vi = np.where(good)[0]
                ti = t[vi]
                pair[vi, ti] = True
        pair &= avail_pad[None, :]
        K = pair.sum(axis=1)

    # --- C[v]: number of solution triples through v whose other two values are both in avail ---
    C = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    avail_vals = np.where(avail)[0] + 1
    if avail_vals.size > 0:
        P = avail_vals
        pp, qq = np.meshgrid(P, P, indexing='ij')
        pp = pp.ravel()
        qq = qq.ravel()
        for (num_fn, den) in (
            (c * pp - a * qq, b),
            (c * pp - b * qq, a),
            (c * qq - a * pp, b),
            (c * qq - b * pp, a),
            (a * pp + b * qq, c),
            (a * qq + b * pp, c),
        ):
            ok = (num_fn % den == 0)
            t = np.where(ok, num_fn // den, -1)
            good = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != pp) & (t != qq)
            tv = t[good]
            tv = tv[avail_pad[tv]]
            np.add.at(C, tv, 1)

    Kc = K[cand].astype(np.float64)
    Cc = C[cand].astype(np.float64)
    out = (Kc - Cc) / (Kc + Cc + 1.0)
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """(1 - position_frac) * (1 - rank of future-partner solution count among candidates) - 0.5, clipped."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    k = cand.shape[0]
    if k == 1:
        return np.zeros(1)

    vals = np.arange(1, n + 1)
    av_idx = np.nonzero(avail)[0] + 1  # values in avail
    C = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=np.int64)

    if av_idx.size >= 2:
        avail_set = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=bool)
        avail_set[av_idx] = True

        # Case 1: v = z, a*x + b*y = c*v
        for x in av_idx:
            num = c * vals - a * x
            valid = (num > 0) & (num % b == 0)
            y = np.where(valid, num // b, -1)
            ok = valid & (y >= 1) & (y <= n)
            yc = np.where(ok, y, 0)
            ok = ok & avail_set[yc] & (yc != x) & (yc != vals)
            C += ok.astype(np.int64)

        # Case 2: v = x, a*v + b*y = c*z  =>  z = (a*v + b*y)/c
        for y in av_idx:
            num = a * vals + b * y
            valid = (num % c == 0)
            z = np.where(valid, num // c, -1)
            ok = valid & (z >= 1) & (z <= n)
            zc = np.where(ok, z, 0)
            ok = ok & avail_set[zc] & (zc != y) & (zc != vals)
            C += ok.astype(np.int64)

        # Case 3: v = y, a*x + b*v = c*z  =>  z = (a*x + b*v)/c
        for x in av_idx:
            num = a * x + b * vals
            valid = (num % c == 0)
            z = np.where(valid, num // c, -1)
            ok = valid & (z >= 1) & (z <= n)
            zc = np.where(ok, z, 0)
            ok = ok & avail_set[zc] & (zc != x) & (zc != vals)
            C += ok.astype(np.int64)

    Ccand = C[cand].astype(np.float64)

    order = np.argsort(Ccand, kind='stable')
    ranks = np.empty(k, dtype=np.float64)
    ranks[order] = np.arange(k, dtype=np.float64)
    r = ranks / max(k - 1, 1)

    p = (cand - 1) / max(n - 1, 1)
    p = np.clip(p, 0.0, 1.0)

    out = (1.0 - p) * (1.0 - r) - 0.5
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Position times local chosen-density excess over global density in a coefficient-scaled window."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    W = max(3, int(round(n / (2.0 * c))))
    cs = np.concatenate(([0], np.cumsum(chosen.astype(np.int64))))
    lo = np.clip(cand - W, 1, n)
    hi = np.clip(cand + W, 1, n)
    cnt = cs[hi] - cs[lo - 1]
    width = (hi - lo + 1).astype(np.float64)
    d = cnt / width
    e = chosen.sum() / float(n)
    p = (cand - 1) / float(max(n - 1, 1))
    return np.clip(3.0 * p * (d - e), -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Killed-available fraction, but only counting kills whose witness s in S is 'isolated' (few S partners), so the count reflects fragile collisions rather than dense clusters."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    m = S.size
    A = np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1
    denom = max(A.size, 1)
    if m == 0 or A.size == 0:
        return np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    # weight for each s in S: inverse of how many candidates-partners it already has in S
    # (s that live in sparse regions of S give more informative kills)
    # count, for each s, the number of t in S sharing a solution with s
    s = S.astype(np.int64)[None, :]
    t = S.astype(np.int64)[:, None]
    shared = np.zeros((m, m), dtype=np.int64)
    # (a*s + b*t)/c integer and in range and distinct
    for num, div in ((a * s + b * t, c), (b * s + a * t, c),
                     (c * s - a * t, b), (c * s - b * t, a)):
        ok = (num % div == 0)
        val = np.where(ok, num // div, -1)
        hit = ok & (val >= 1) & (val <= n) & (val != s) & (val != t)
        shared += hit.astype(np.int64)
    np.fill_diagonal(shared, 0)
    deg = shared.sum(axis=0).astype(float)  # per s (column = s)
    w_s = 1.0 / (1.0 + deg)  # isolated s -> weight near 1

    v = cand[:, None]                        # (k,1)
    srow = S[None, :]                        # (1,m)
    K = np.zeros((k, n), dtype=float)        # weighted kills per (cand, w)

    def mark(num, div):
        ok = (num % div == 0)
        tt = np.where(ok, num // div, 0)
        valid = ok & (tt >= 1) & (tt <= n)
        rows, cols = np.nonzero(valid)
        wv = tt[rows, cols] - 1
        np.add.at(K, (rows, wv), np.broadcast_to(w_s, (k, m))[rows, cols])

    mark(a * v + b * srow, c)
    mark(b * v + a * srow, c)
    mark(c * v - a * srow, b)
    mark(c * v - b * srow, a)
    mark(c * srow - a * v, b)
    mark(c * srow - b * v, a)

    K[np.arange(k), cand - 1] = 0.0
    K *= avail[None, :]

    # number of distinct available w hit (weighted by isolation) 
    hit = (K > 0).astype(float)
    weighted = (K * hit).sum(axis=1)
    return np.tanh(weighted / denom)

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Resonance measured only against the closest few chosen neighbours: mean over the K=6 nearest s in S of cos(2*pi*a*(v-s)/c) and cos(2*pi*b*(v-s)/c), averaged, clipped to [-1,1]."""

    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    m = S.size
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    if m == 0:
        return out

    K = min(6, m)
    # For each candidate, find the K nearest members of S by |v - s|.
    # Vectorised: distances (k, m)
    v = cand[:, None]                    # (k,1)
    s = S[None, :]                       # (1,m)
    d = np.abs(v - s)                    # (k,m)

    idx = np.argpartition(d, K - 1, axis=1)[:, :K]  # (k,K)
    s_near = s[0, idx]                   # (k,K) chosen neighbour values

    diff = (v - s_near).astype(float)    # (k,K)
    ca = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * a * diff / c)
    cb = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * b * diff / c)
    score = 0.5 * (ca.mean(axis=1) + cb.mean(axis=1))
    return np.clip(score, -1.0, 1.0)

    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    m = S.size
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    if m < 1:
        return out
    if np.count_nonzero(avail) <= 1:
        return out

    v = cand[:, None]
    Srow = S[None, :]

    # form A: x=v, y=s, z=(a*v+b*s)/c
    num = a * v + b * Srow
    ok = (num % c == 0)
    t = np.where(ok, num // c, 0)
    valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
    tc = np.where(valid, t, 1) - 1
    tc = np.clip(tc, 0, n - 1)
    cntA = (valid & avail[tc]).sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    # form B: x=s, y=v, z=(a*s+b*v)/c
    num = a * Srow + b * v
    ok = (num % c == 0)
    t = np.where(ok, num // c, 0)
    valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
    tc = np.clip(np.where(valid, t, 1) - 1, 0, n - 1)
    cntB = (valid & avail[tc]).sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    # form C: z=v, y=(c*v-a*s)/b
    num = c * v - a * Srow
    ok = (num % b == 0)
    t = np.where(ok, num // b, 0)
    valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
    tc = np.clip(np.where(valid, t, 1) - 1, 0, n - 1)
    cntC = (valid & avail[tc]).sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    # form D: z=v, x=(c*v-b*s)/a
    num = c * v - b * Srow
    ok = (num % a == 0)
    t = np.where(ok, num // a, 0)
    valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
    tc = np.clip(np.where(valid, t, 1) - 1, 0, n - 1)
    cntD = (valid & avail[tc]).sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    total = cntA + cntB + cntC + cntD
    return np.tanh(total / (float(m) + 1.0))

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Signed parity-split kill mass: (2*K_same - K)/(K+1), K = available numbers killed by candidate."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    v = cand[:, None].astype(np.int64)          # (k,1)
    s = S[None, :].astype(np.int64)             # (1,|S|)
    k = cand.shape[0]
    killmask = np.zeros((k, n), dtype=bool)

    completions = [
        (a * v + b * s, c),
        (c * s - a * v, b),
        (a * s + b * v, c),
        (c * s - b * v, a),
        (c * v - a * s, b),
        (c * v - b * s, a),
    ]

        valid = (N % d == 0)
        if not valid.any():
            continue
        t = N // d
        ok = valid & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != v)
        if not ok.any():
            continue
        rows, _ = np.nonzero(ok)
        cols = t[ok] - 1

    parity = (np.arange(1, n + 1) % 2)[None, :] == (cand % 2)[:, None]
    K_same = (killmask & parity).sum(1).astype(np.float64)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Fraction of still-available numbers that survive adding v and are themselves cheap (own kill count <= median)."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    A = np.flatnonzero(avail)  # available numbers, sorted
    m = A.size
    if m == 0:
        return np.zeros(cand.shape[0])

    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen)
    coefs = (a, b, -c)
    perms = [(0, 1, 2), (0, 2, 1), (1, 0, 2), (1, 2, 0), (2, 0, 1), (2, 1, 0)]

    def killmask(cands):
        k = cands.size
        mask = np.zeros((k, n), dtype=bool)
        if S.size == 0 or k == 0:
            return mask
        for s in S:
            for pv, pw, ps in perms:
                cv = coefs[pv]
                cw = coefs[pw]
                cs = coefs[ps]
                if cw == 0:
                    continue
                num = -(cv * cands + cs * s)
                # divisibility check (vectorised, safe for negatives)
                rem = np.mod(num, cw)
                div_ok = (rem == 0)
                if not np.any(div_ok):
                    continue
                w = num // cw
                valid = div_ok & (w >= 1) & (w <= n) & (w != cands) & (w != s)
                rows = np.flatnonzero(valid)
                if rows.size:
                    mask[rows, w[rows] - 1] = True
        return mask

    # First pass: kill counts over A
    killA = killmask(A)
    Kw = killA.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    thr = np.median(Kw)
    cheap = Kw <= thr

    # Second pass: killmask for candidates
    killV = killmask(cand)
    Kv = killV[:, A - 1].copy()
    # candidate counts itself as removed
    for i in range(cand.size):
        idx = np.searchsorted(A, cand[i])
        if idx < m and A[idx] == cand[i]:
            Kv[i, idx] = True
    survivors = ~Kv
    counts = (survivors & cheap[None, :]).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    out = counts / max(m, 1)
    return np.clip(out, 0.0, 1.0)

    """Saturating balance K/(K+1) - C/(C+1): K = live numbers killed by adding v, C = live-threat solutions created by v."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1          # shape (m,)
    A = np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1           # shape (p,)
    v = cand[:, None]                       # shape (k,1)
    k = cand.shape[0]

        t = np.where(ok, num // c, 0)
        ok &= (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
        tt = np.clip(t, 1, n)
        ok &= avail[tt - 1]
        ok &= (tt != v)
        if extra_self:

        ok &= (tt != v)
        if extra_self:

        total += ok.sum(1)

        num = c * s - b * v

        if extra_self:

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Position coupled with crowding: candidate position times local density of S in a window around it, normalised to [-1,1]."""
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    pos = np.clip((cand - 1) / float(max(n - 1, 1)), 0.0, 1.0)
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    if S.size == 0:
        return 2.0 * pos - 1.0
    S = S.astype(np.int64)
    W = max(3, int(round(0.15 * n)))
    # local density of chosen numbers within +/- W of each candidate, using sorted S and searchsorted
    Ss = np.sort(S)
    lo = np.searchsorted(Ss, cand - W, side='left')
    hi = np.searchsorted(Ss, cand + W, side='right')
    dens = (hi - lo).astype(float) / float(2 * W + 1)
    dens = np.clip(dens, 0.0, 1.0)
    # interaction: candidate near the low end but in a crowded region should be penalised more
    score = (1.0 - pos) * dens - pos * (1.0 - dens)
    return np.clip(score, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Ratio of frontier-weighted kill mass (near 1..n edges) to bulk-weighted kill mass produced when adding each candidate; bounded in [-1,1]."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.shape[0]
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    if S.size == 0 or k == 0:
        return out

    v = cand[:, None].astype(np.int64)      # (k,1)
    s = S[None, :].astype(np.int64)         # (1,m)
    edge = 6

    def edge_weight(t):
        d = np.minimum(t - 1, n - t).astype(np.float64)
        return np.clip(1.0 - d / edge, 0.0, 1.0)

    edge_mass = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    bulk_mass = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    tt = [
        (a * v + b * s, c),
        (b * v + a * s, c),
        (c * v - b * s, a),
        (c * v - a * s, b),
    ]
    for num, den in tt:
        ok = (num % den == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // den, 0)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
        tc = np.clip(t, 1, n)
        hit = valid & (tc != v) & (tc != s) & avail[tc - 1]
        hf = hit.astype(np.float64)
        w = edge_weight(tc.astype(np.float64))
        edge_mass += (hf * w).sum(axis=1)
        bulk_mass += (hf * (1.0 - w)).sum(axis=1)

    # ratio: high when frontier-weighted portion dominates bulk part
    total = edge_mass + bulk_mass
    ratio = np.where(total > 0, (edge_mass - bulk_mass) / (total + 1e-9), 0.0)
    return np.tanh(ratio)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Kill mass of candidate vs. a distance-matched null: neighbours of v in S weighted by 1/(1+|v-s|), compared to uniform exposure, normalised."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.shape[0]
    m = int(np.count_nonzero(chosen))
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    if S.size == 0 or k == 0:
        return out

    v = cand[:, None].astype(np.float64)   # (k,1)
    s = S[None, :].astype(np.float64)      # (1,|S|)
    # distance weighting: nearby chosen numbers matter more for forced completions
    wgt = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.abs(v - s))      # (k,|S|)

    mass = np.zeros((k,), dtype=np.float64)
    t1 = (a * v + b * s) / c
    t2 = (b * v + a * s) / c
    t3 = (c * v - b * s) / a
    t4 = (c * v - a * s) / b
    for t in (t1, t2, t3, t4):
        ti = np.rint(t)
        is_int = np.abs(t - ti) < 1e-9
        ti_i = ti.astype(np.int64)
        in_range = is_int & (ti_i >= 1) & (ti_i <= n)
        ti_clip = np.clip(ti_i, 1, n)
        not_v = ti_i != cand[:, None]
        not_s = ti_i != S[None, :]
        av = avail[ti_clip - 1]
        hit = in_range & not_v & not_s & av
        mass += (hit * wgt).sum(axis=1)

    # state-free exposure: expected forced completions in a uniform S, distance-weighted
    # average weight of a random partner over 1..n scales like (2 log n)/n; use m times that
    avg_w = (2.0 * np.log(n + 1.0)) / max(n, 1)
    exp = 4.0 * m * avg_w
    return np.clip((mass - exp) / (1.0 + exp), -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Share of still-available numbers whose add would be blocked by candidate together with some s in S, measured only over the upper half of the range (cand>n/2)."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    m = S.size
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    if m == 0:
        return out

    # restrict blocking partners to upper half of range
    A = (np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    upper = A[A > n // 2]
    nU = max(upper.size, 1)

    v = cand[:, None]
    s = S[None, :]

    K = np.zeros((k, n), dtype=bool)

    def mark(num, mod, denom):
        ok = (num % mod == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // denom if denom != mod else num // mod, 0)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
        rows, cols = np.nonzero(valid)
        if rows.size:
            K[rows, t[rows, cols] - 1] = True

    # partner in the (x,y) slot, third value t
    mark(a * v + b * s, c, c)   # t = (a*v+b*s)/c
    mark(b * v + a * s, c, c)   # t = (b*v+a*s)/c
    mark(c * v - a * s, b, b)   # t = (c*v-a*s)/b
    mark(c * v - b * s, a, a)   # t = (c*v-b*s)/a
    mark(c * s - a * v, b, b)   # t = (c*s-a*v)/b
    mark(c * s - b * v, a, a)   # t = (c*s-b*v)/a

    K[np.arange(k), cand - 1] = False

    # only count blocked numbers that lie in upper half
    up_mask = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    up_mask[upper - 1] = True
    K &= up_mask[None, :]

    return K.sum(axis=1).astype(float) / nU

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Position fraction modulated by local chosen-density just below v: (cand-1)/(n-1) times (1 - local_density_scale)."""
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    pos = np.clip((cand - 1) / float(n - 1), 0.0, 1.0)
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    if S.size == 0:
        return pos
    Ssort = np.sort(S.astype(np.int64))
    # window width grows with n; count chosen below v within window
    W = max(3, int(round(0.12 * n)))
    # for each candidate count chosen in (v - W, v)
    lo = np.searchsorted(Ssort, cand - W, side='left')
    hi = np.searchsorted(Ssort, cand - 1, side='right')
    below = (hi - lo).astype(float)
    # and chosen just above (v, v+W)
    lo2 = np.searchsorted(Ssort, cand, side='left')
    hi2 = np.searchsorted(Ssort, cand + W, side='right')
    above = (hi2 - lo2).astype(float)
    dens = (below - above) / float(W)  # in [-1,1] roughly: dense below -> positive
    dens = np.tanh(dens)
    # high position but sparse below: reward; dense below: demote
    return np.clip(pos * (1.0 + 0.5 * dens), -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """m/(1+m) with m = P/(1+K): mean number of chosen witnesses per distinct threatening available number, squashed to [0,1)."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    k = cand.shape[0]
    S = np.nonzero(chosen)[0] + 1  # chosen numbers, shape (m,)
    m = S.shape[0]
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    if m == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    v = cand.astype(np.int64)          # (k,)
    s = S.astype(np.int64)             # (m,)
    V = v[:, None]                     # (k,1)
    Ss = s[None, :]                    # (1,m)

    # six formulas: (numerator, denominator) as arrays shape (k,m)
    nums = [
        (c * Ss - a * V, b),   # v=X, w=Y
        (c * Ss - b * V, a),   # v=Y, w=X
        (a * V + b * Ss, c),   # v=X, w=Z
        (b * V + a * Ss, c),   # v=Y, w=Z
        (c * V - b * Ss, a),   # v=Z, w=X
        (c * V - a * Ss, b),   # v=Z, w=Y
    ]

    P = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.int64)
    counts = np.zeros((k, n + 1), dtype=np.int64)

    for num, den in nums:
        if den == 0:
            continue
        exact = (num % den) == 0
        w = num // den
        valid = exact & (w >= 1) & (w <= n)
        # w != v and w != s
        valid &= (w != V) & (w != Ss)
        # avail[w-1] True
        wc = np.clip(w, 1, n)
        valid &= avail[wc - 1]
        # accumulate
        P += valid.sum(axis=1)
        idx = np.nonzero(valid)
        if idx[0].size:
            rows = idx[0]
            ws = w[idx]
            flat = rows * (n + 1) + ws
            counts += np.bincount(flat, minlength=k * (n + 1)).reshape(k, n + 1)

    K = (counts > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)
    Pf = P.astype(np.float64)
    mean = Pf / (1.0 + K)
    return mean / (1.0 + mean)

idea.hypothesis: Threat to v and kills by v are the same relation (w blocks v iff {v,w} plus a witness s in S is a solution), so the plain killer COUNT is already f026. What is unmeasured is the DEPTH of the threat: how many chosen witnesses support each threatening available number. A candidate with many killers, each with one witness, is differently placed from one with the same number of killers each witnessed several ways. Returning the mean witnesses per killer isolates depth from count.
idea.feature: One column. Six exact-division formulas per (v, s) with s in S: v=X,w=Y -> w=(c*s-a*v)/b; v=Y,w=X -> w=(c*s-b*v)/a; v=X,w=Z -> w=(a*v+b*s)/c; v=Y,w=Z -> w=(b*v+a*s)/c; v=Z,w=X -> w=(c*v-b*s)/a; v=Z,w=Y -> w=(c*v-a*s)/b. import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Mean over killed available numbers w of K(w)/(1+K(w)), where K(w) = number of candidates that would kill w."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    k = cand.shape[0]
    v = cand.astype(np.int64)  # (k,)
    S = np.nonzero(chosen)[0].astype(np.int64) + 1  # (m,)
    m = S.shape[0]

    # flat index array of shape (k*(n+1)) for dedupe via np.maximum
    total = k * (n + 1)
    flat = np.zeros(total, dtype=np.int8)

    if m > 0:
        V = v[:, None]      # (k,1)
        Sm = S[None, :]     # (1,m)
        rows = np.arange(k, dtype=np.int64)[:, None]  # (k,1)

        # six formulas: (num, den) with w = num/den
        # 1) w=(c*s-a*v)/b
        # 2) w=(c*s-b*v)/a
        # 3) w=(a*v+b*s)/c
        # 4) w=(b*v+a*s)/c
        # 5) w=(c*v-b*s)/a
        # 6) w=(c*v-a*s)/b
        formulas = [
            (c * Sm - a * V, b),
            (c * Sm - b * V, a),
            (a * V + b * Sm, c),
            (b * V + a * Sm, c),
            (c * V - b * Sm, a),
            (c * V - a * Sm, b),
        ]

        for num, den in formulas:
            if den == 0:
                continue
            exact = (num % den) == 0
            w = num // den
            valid = exact & (w >= 1) & (w <= n) & (w != V) & (w != Sm)
            # avail check: avail[w-1] True
            wc = np.clip(w, 1, n)
            valid = valid & avail[wc - 1]
            # also w must not equal the candidate itself (already w!=V) and not s (w!=Sm)
            idx = rows * (n + 1) + wc
            flat[np.where(valid, idx, 0).ravel()] = np.where(valid.ravel(), 1, flat[np.where(valid, idx, 0).ravel()])

    M = flat.reshape(k, n + 1).astype(np.int64)
    colsum = M.sum(axis=0)  # K(w) for w in 0..n
    K = colsum.astype(np.float64)
    weight = K / (1.0 + K)  # (n+1,)
    rowsum = M.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)  # (k,)
    num = M @ weight  # (k,)
    out = np.where(rowsum > 0, num / np.maximum(1.0, rowsum), 0.0)
    return np.clip(out, 0.0, 1.0 - 1e-9)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Two columns: (1) 1/c minus the share of S in the candidate's residue class mod c; (2) normalised distance from the candidate to the nearest chosen number in its residue class mod c (1.0 if none)."""
    c = int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.shape[0]
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1  # chosen values in 1..n
    nS = S.shape[0]

    # Column 1: class occupancy deficit
    if nS == 0:
        col1 = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    else:
        S_res = S % c
        cand_res = cand % c
        # count chosen in each residue class
        counts = np.bincount(S_res, minlength=c).astype(np.float64)
        share = counts[cand_res] / float(nS)
        col1 = (1.0 / c) - share

    # Column 2: nearest congruent chosen distance, normalised
    scale = float(n) / float(c)
    if scale <= 0:

    col2 = np.ones(k, dtype=np.float64)
    if nS > 0:
        S_res = S % c
        cand_res = cand % c
        # group chosen by residue

        S_sorted = S[order]
        S_res_sorted = S_res[order]
        # boundaries of each residue group

        # build unique residues and start/end indices

        ends = np.append(starts[1:], nS)
        # map candidate residue to group index (-1 if absent)

        pos_clipped = np.clip(pos, 0, uniq.shape[0] - 1)
        present = uniq[pos_clipped] == cand_res

                continue
            g = pos_clipped[i]

            col2[i] = min(1.0, float(d) / scale)

        col2 = np.ones(k, dtype=np.float64)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Position of candidate relative to the chosen set's density: low when the candidate sits in a sparse region (few chosen neighbours in a window around it), so it prefers numbers in under-used intervals; zero when S is empty."""
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    if S.size == 0:
        return np.zeros(cand.shape[0], dtype=float)
    # window width scales with n and current density
    W = max(3, int(round(0.12 * n)))
    Ssort = np.sort(S.astype(np.int64))
    lo = np.searchsorted(Ssort, cand - W, side='left')
    hi = np.searchsorted(Ssort, cand + W, side='right')
    local_count = (hi - lo).astype(float)
    # expected local count if S were spread uniformly over 1..n
    expected = S.size * (2.0 * W) / float(n)
    expected = max(expected, 1e-9)
    # sparse (negative) when local density below expectation, dense (positive) above
    return np.tanh((local_count - expected) / expected)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Share of available numbers killed by the candidate, weighted by how scarce each killed number is (1/(local avail density)), and by whether the kill comes from a high-count (conflict-dense) third value; rewards sparse-region candidates."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    k = cand.shape[0]
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    m = S.size
    if m == 0:
        return np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    A = np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1
    nA = max(A.size, 1)

    # local availability density over a sliding window (window = max(3, n//20))
    W = max(3, n // 20)
    dens = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=float)
    av = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=float)
    av[1:n + 1] = avail[:n].astype(float)
    csum = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(av[1:n + 1])])
    for v in range(1, n + 1):
        lo = max(1, v - W)
        hi = min(n, v + W)
        dens[v] = (csum[hi] - csum[lo - 1]) / float(hi - lo + 1)

    v = cand.astype(np.int64)[:, None]
    s = S.astype(np.int64)[None, :]

    K = np.zeros((k, n), dtype=bool)

    def mark(num, mod, mul_ok_mask=None):
        ok = (num % mod == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // mod, 0)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
        rows, cols = np.nonzero(valid)
        K[rows, t[rows, cols] - 1] = True

    mark(a * v + b * s, c)
    mark(b * v + a * s, c)
    mark(c * v - a * s, b)
    mark(c * v - b * s, a)
    mark(c * s - a * v, b)
    mark(c * s - b * v, a)

    K[np.arange(k), cand.astype(np.int64) - 1] = False
    K &= avail[None, :]

    # weight each killed number by inverse local density (scarce -> kill hurts more)
    w = 1.0 / (dens[1:n + 1] + 1.0 / nA)
    weighted = (K.astype(float) * w[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
    # also count raw kills, scaled
    raw = K.sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    score = 0.5 * (weighted / (nA * (1.0 / nA) * nA + 1.0)) + 0.5 * (raw / nA)
    return np.tanh(score)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """For each candidate, the number of solutions it would create whose OTHER two slots are chosen (in S) summed over multi-step completions one level deeper: solutions v can form where one partner is in S and the third is addable, weighted by how many solutions that addable third already has with S."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    m = S.size
    if m == 0:
        return np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    av = np.zeros(n + 2, dtype=bool)
    av[1:n + 1] = avail[:n]

    density = m / max(n, 1)
    expected = density * density * n

    # Precompute, for every addable number w, how many solutions w forms with S
    # (partner in S, third slot addable) -- this is the "danger" of w.
    A = np.flatnonzero(av[:n]) + 1  # addable numbers
    danger = np.zeros(n + 2, dtype=float)
    if A.size > 0:
        w = A[:, None].astype(np.int64)
        s = S[None, :].astype(np.int64)
        # count completions with third slot addable, excluding w and s
        cnt_w = np.zeros(A.size, dtype=float)
        # role x=w: t=(a*w+b*s)/c
        for coef_k, coef_o, denom in ((a, b, c), (b, a, c)):
            num = coef_k * w + coef_o * s
            okm = (num % denom == 0)
            t = np.where(okm, num // denom, -1)
            valid = okm & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != w) & (s != w) & (s != t)
            tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
            cnt_w += (valid & av[tc]).sum(axis=1)
        # role z=w: t=(c*w - a*s)/b and (c*w - b*s)/a
        for coef_k, coef_o, denom in ((a, b, None), (b, a, None)):
            num = c * w - coef_k * s
            okm = (num % coef_o == 0)
            t = np.where(okm, num // coef_o, -1)
            valid = okm & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != w) & (s != w) & (s != t)
            tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
            cnt_w += (valid & av[tc]).sum(axis=1)
        danger[A] = cnt_w

    v = cand[:, None].astype(np.int64)
    Srow = S[None, :].astype(np.int64)

    # For each candidate v, for each completion where a partner s in S and third slot t is
    # addable, add danger[t] -- i.e. how dangerous the addable third would become.
    score = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    for coef_k, coef_o, denom in ((a, b, c), (b, a, c)):
        num = coef_k * v + coef_o * Srow
        okm = (num % denom == 0)
        t = np.where(okm, num // denom, -1)
        valid = okm & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != v) & (Srow != v) & (Srow != t)
        tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
        score += (valid & av[tc]).dot(danger[tc] if False else 0) if False else 0  # placeholder
    # vectorised gather of danger
    for coef_k, coef_o, denom in ((a, b, c), (b, a, c)):
        num = coef_k * v + coef_o * Srow
        okm = (num % denom == 0)
        t = np.where(okm, num // denom, -1)
        valid = okm & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != v) & (Srow != v) & (Srow != t)
        tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
        contrib = np.where(valid & av[tc], danger[tc], 0.0)
        score += contrib.sum(axis=1)
    for coef_k, coef_o in ((a, b), (b, a)):
        num = c * v - coef_k * Srow
        okm = (num % coef_o == 0)
        t = np.where(okm, num // coef_o, -1)
        valid = okm & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != v) & (Srow != v) & (Srow != t)
        tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
        contrib = np.where(valid & av[tc], danger[tc], 0.0)
        score += contrib.sum(axis=1)

    denom_scale = (expected * expected) + score
    return np.where(denom_scale > 0, score / denom_scale, 0.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """For each candidate: the fraction of available numbers w whose addability would be *newly blocked* (become non-addable) once v is added, counting only w that survive the immediate S-conflict test but would then be pushed into a solution with v and another surviving number."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    A = (np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    if S.size == 0 or A.size == 0:
        return out

    Amask = avail
    av_idx = np.zeros(n + 2, dtype=bool)
    av_idx[1:n + 1] = avail[:n]

    v = cand[:, None]           # (k,1)
    Srow = S[None, :]           # (1,m)

    # For candidate v, mark all numbers t (1..n) that would conflict with v+S (i.e. become
    # unable to be added because they'd complete a solution with v and some s in S).
    K = np.zeros((k, n), dtype=bool)

    def mark(num, mod, sign_rows):
        ok = (num % mod == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // mod, 0)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
        r, cidx = np.nonzero(valid)
        K[r, t[r, cidx] - 1] = True

    # t = (a*v + b*s)/c
    mark(a * v + b * Srow, c, None)
    # t = (b*v + a*s)/c
    mark(b * v + a * Srow, c, None)
    # t = (c*v - a*s)/b
    mark(c * v - a * Srow, b, None)
    # t = (c*v - b*s)/a
    mark(c * v - b * Srow, a, None)
    # t = (c*s - a*v)/b
    mark(c * Srow - a * v, b, None)
    # t = (c*s - b*v)/a
    mark(c * Srow - b * v, a, None)

    K[np.arange(k), cand - 1] = False

    # was t already blocked by S alone?  (then adding v doesn't newly block it)
    SB = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    if S.size > 0:
        def markS(num, mod):
            ok = (num % mod == 0)
            t = np.where(ok, num // mod, 0)
            valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
            SB[t[valid] - 1] = True
        s2 = S[None, :]
        markS(a * s2 + b * s2.T, c)
        markS(c * s2 - a * s2.T, b)
        markS(c * s2 - b * s2.T, a)

    # only count w that are still available and not already blocked by S
    newly = K & Amask[None, :] & (~SB)[None, :]
    cnt = newly.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    denom = max(A.size - 1, 1)
    return np.tanh(cnt / denom)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Mean over addable w of the fraction of S-partners of v that are also S-partners of w (partner-set overlap), tanh-normalised."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    A = (np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    if S.size == 0 or A.size == 0 or k == 0:
        return out

    v = cand[:, None]
    s = S[None, :]

    # pairV[v, s]: True if (v, s) admit some completion t in avail, t distinct from v and s
    pairV = np.zeros((k, S.size), dtype=bool)

    def markV(num, denom):
        ok = (num % denom == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // denom, 0)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != v) & (t != s)
        tc = np.clip(t, 1, n)
        valid = valid & avail[tc - 1]
        pairV |= valid

    markV(a * v + b * s, c)
    markV(b * v + a * s, c)
    markV(c * s - a * v, b)
    markV(c * s - b * v, a)
    markV(c * v - a * s, b)
    markV(c * v - b * s, a)

    # pairW[w, s]: True if (w, s) admit some completion t in avail, t distinct from w and s
    Wv = A[:, None]
    Sv = S[None, :]
    pairW = np.zeros((A.size, S.size), dtype=bool)

    def markW(num, denom):
        ok = (num % denom == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // denom, 0)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != Wv) & (t != Sv)
        tc = np.clip(t, 1, n)
        valid = valid & avail[tc - 1]
        pairW |= valid

    markW(a * Wv + b * Sv, c)
    markW(b * Wv + a * Sv, c)
    markW(c * Sv - a * Wv, b)
    markW(c * Sv - b * Wv, a)
    markW(c * Wv - a * Sv, b)
    markW(c * Wv - b * Sv, a)

    # intersection counts per (v, w) over s
    inter = pairV.astype(np.int32) @ pairW.T.astype(np.int32)  # (k, A.size)
    # normalise each pair by |pairV_v| (fraction of v's partners shared with w), avoid div by zero
    denomV = pairV.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)  # (k,)
    denomV = np.where(denomV > 0, denomV, 1.0)
    frac = inter / denomV[:, None]  # (k, A.size)
    overlap = frac.mean(axis=1)
    return np.tanh(overlap)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """2*frac - 1 where frac = share of the 5 largest available numbers (excluding v) that remain addable after adding v."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    k = cand.shape[0]
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    avail_vals = np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1  # currently addable values, sorted
    if avail_vals.size == 0:
        return out

    # The 5 largest available numbers overall (excluding v per-candidate below).
    top5 = avail_vals[-5:] if avail_vals.size >= 5 else avail_vals
    m = top5.size

    # For each candidate v, T = top5 with v removed (v is in avail, may be in top5).
    # Build T matrix: shape (k, m) with v replaced by a sentinel (0) then compacted.
    T = np.tile(top5, (k, 1))  # (k, m)
    T[T == cand[:, None]] = 0  # mark v's slot as 0 (invalid)

    # S' = S + {v}: for each candidate, membership differs only by v.
    # We'll evaluate "still addable" for each (candidate, t) pair vectorised over t.
    # t is not in S' (t is available, t != v), so distinctness from t is automatic.
    # Need: exists x,y in S' with x!=y and a*x+b*y = c*t  (t as z)
    #    or exists y,z in S' with y!=z and a*t+b*y = c*z  (t as x)
    #    or exists x,z in S' with x!=z and a*x+b*t = c*z  (t as y)

    S_vals = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1  # sorted chosen values
    # S' membership: chosen plus v. We'll handle v separately.

    # Precompute for the base set S (without v):
    # For t as z: need a*x + b*y = c*t with x,y in S' (x!=y).
    # For t as x: need a*t + b*y = c*z with y,z in S' (y!=z).
    # For t as y: need a*x + b*t = c*z with x,z in S' (x!=z).
    # We vectorise over (candidate, t) pairs: shape (k, m).

    Tv = T  # (k, m), 0 means invalid slot
    valid = Tv > 0  # (k, m)

    # Build S' membership as a boolean array per candidate is expensive (k x n).
    # Instead, note S' = S ∪ {v}. For a value w, w in S' iff chosen[w-1] or w == v.
    # We'll compute membership via searchsorted on S_vals and explicit v check.

    def in_Sprime(w, v):
        # w: array, v: array (broadcastable). Returns bool array.
        idx = np.searchsorted(S_vals, w)
        idx = np.clip(idx, 0, S_vals.size - 1) if S_vals.size > 0 else np.zeros_like(w)
        inS = (S_vals.size > 0) & (S_vals[idx] == w) if S_vals.size > 0 else np.zeros_like(w, dtype=bool)
        return inS | (w == v)

    # We need, for each (i, j) with valid[i,j], to test existence of a partner.
    # Vectorise over the (k, m) grid using the structure of the equation.

    # Case t as z: a*x + b*y = c*t, x,y in S', x != y.
    # For each x in S', y = (c*t - a*x)/b must be in S', integer, y != x.
    # We iterate over x in S' (size |S|+1) — that's a loop over set elements, not candidates.
    # But we can vectorise over the (k, m) grid for each x.

    # To keep it fast, iterate over x in S_vals (plus v handled separately), vectorised over grid.

    still = np.zeros((k, m), dtype=bool)

    # Helper: check membership of array w in S' for candidate v (array over grid)
    def member(w, v):
        # w: (k, m) int array, v: (k, 1) int
        if S_vals.size == 0:
            return (w == v)
        idx = np.searchsorted(S_vals, w)
        idx_c = np.clip(idx, 0, S_vals.size - 1)
        inS = (S_vals[idx_c] == w)
        return inS | (w == v)

    v_col = cand[:, None]  # (k, 1)

    # Case t as z: iterate x over S_vals
    for x in S_vals:
        num = c * Tv - a * x  # (k, m)
        # y = num / b must be integer
        ok_div = (num % b == 0) & valid
        y = num // b
        ok = ok_div & (y != x) & member(y, v_col)
        still |= ok

    # Also x could be v itself (v in S')
    num = c * Tv - a * v_col
    ok_div = (num % b == 0) & valid
    y = num // b
    ok = ok_div & (y != v_col) & member(y, v_col)
    still |= ok

    # Case t as x: a*t + b*y = c*z, y,z in S', y != z.
    # Iterate y over S_vals
    for y in S_vals:
        num = a * Tv + b * y  # (k, m)
        ok_div = (num % c == 0) & valid
        z = num // c
        ok = ok_div & (z != y) & member(z, v_col)
        still |= ok
    # y could be v
    num = a * Tv + b * v_col
    ok_div = (num % c == 0) & valid
    z = num // c
    ok = ok_div & (z != v_col) & member(z, v_col)
    still |= ok

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """1 - 2 * share of available u for which (v,u) completes a triple with an addable z, over six role assignments."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.shape[0]
    idx = np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1  # available values
    m = idx.shape[0]
    if m == 0 or k == 0:
        return np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)

    v = cand[:, None]          # (k,1)
    u = idx[None, :]           # (1,m)

    counts = np.zeros((k, m), dtype=bool)

    def check(num, den):
        if den == 0:
            return np.zeros((k, m), dtype=bool)
        valid = (num % den) == 0
        z = np.where(valid, num // np.where(den == 0, 1, den), 0)
        inrange = valid & (z >= 1) & (z <= n)
        zc = np.clip(z, 1, n)
        distinct = inrange & (zc != v) & (zc != u)
        addable = distinct & avail[zc - 1]
        return addable

    counts |= check(a * v + b * u, c)
    counts |= check(a * u + b * v, c)
    if b != 0:
        counts |= check(c * u - a * v, b)
    if a != 0:
        counts |= check(c * u - b * v, a)
    if b != 0:
        counts |= check(c * v - a * u, b)
    if a != 0:
        counts |= check(c * v - b * u, a)

    share = counts.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64) / float(m)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """1 - 2 * (sum of residual pair-degree over numbers killed by adding v) / (total residual pair-degree over avail + 1)."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    k = cand.shape[0]
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)

    avail_idx = np.nonzero(avail)[0] + 1  # values t in avail
    m = avail_idx.shape[0]
    if m == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    # Residual pair-degree over avail: ordered pairs (t,u), t != u, with a valid
    # third z in avail distinct from both.
    T = avail_idx[:, None]
    U = avail_idx[None, :]
    num = a * T + b * U
    z = num // c
    rem = num - z * c
    valid = (rem == 0) & (z >= 1) & (z <= n)
    zc = np.clip(z, 1, n)
    valid &= avail[zc - 1]
    valid &= (zc != T) & (zc != U)
    valid &= (T != U)
    deg = valid.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)  # (m,)

    total = deg.sum() + 1.0

    deg_lookup = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=np.float64)
    deg_lookup[avail_idx] = deg

    S_vals = np.nonzero(chosen)[0] + 1

    result = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)

    if S_vals.shape[0] > 0:
        Sv = S_vals.astype(np.int64)
        for i in range(k):
            v = int(cand[i])
            killed = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=bool)

            num1 = a * v + b * Sv
            z1 = num1 // c
            ok1 = (num1 % c == 0) & (z1 >= 1) & (z1 <= n)

            num2 = a * Sv + b * v
            z2 = num2 // c
            ok2 = (num2 % c == 0) & (z2 >= 1) & (z2 <= n)

            num3 = c * Sv - a * v
            y3 = num3 // b
            ok3 = (num3 % b == 0) & (y3 >= 1) & (y3 <= n)

            num4 = c * Sv - b * v
            x4 = num4 // a
            ok4 = (num4 % a == 0) & (x4 >= 1) & (x4 <= n)

            num5 = c * v - a * Sv
            y5 = num5 // b
            ok5 = (num5 % b == 0) & (y5 >= 1) & (y5 <= n)

            num6 = c * v - b * Sv
            x6 = num6 // a
            ok6 = (num6 % a == 0) & (x6 >= 1) & (x6 <= n)

            for arr, ok in ((z1, ok1), (z2, ok2), (y3, ok3), (x4, ok4), (y5, ok5), (x6, ok6)):

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Position in [-1,1] for candidates that strand nothing in the top 10% of the addable pool, else 0."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    k = cand.shape[0]
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    A = np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1
    Asorted = np.sort(A)

    pos = 2.0 * (cand - 1) / max(n - 1, 1) - 1.0

    if S.size == 0:
        return pos

    Sarr = np.sort(S)
    uf = Sarr.astype(np.float64)

    nP = A.size - 1
    nT = max(1, int(np.ceil(0.10 * nP)))
    top_all = Asorted[::-1]

    hits_per_cand = np.zeros(k, dtype=bool)

    for idx in range(k):
        v = int(cand[idx])
        vf = float(v)
        hit = set()

        cands_t = [
            (c * uf - b * vf) / a,
            (c * vf - b * uf) / a,
            (c * uf - a * vf) / b,
            (c * vf - a * uf) / b,
            (a * vf + b * uf) / c,
            (a * uf + b * vf) / c,
        ]

        for tvals in cands_t:
            ti = np.round(tvals)
            ok = np.abs(tvals - ti) < 1e-9
            ti = ti[ok].astype(np.int64)
            if ti.size == 0:
                continue
            u_ok = Sarr[ok]
            valid = (ti >= 1) & (ti <= n) & (ti != v) & (ti != u_ok)
            p = np.clip(np.searchsorted(Asorted, ti), 0, Asorted.size - 1)
            valid &= (Asorted[p] == ti)
            ti = ti[valid]
            if ti.size:
                hit.update(ti.tolist())

        if not hit:
            continue

        if v in top_all[:nT]:
            T = [int(x) for x in top_all[:nT + 1] if x != v]
        else:
            T = [int(x) for x in top_all[:nT]]

        if any(t in hit for t in T):
            hits_per_cand[idx] = True

    return np.where(hits_per_cand, 0.0, pos)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Kill-impact of a candidate weighted by how much future each killed number w loses, measured by w's partner count within the remaining addable set (hub score), so killing hubs hurts more than killing leaves."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen).astype(np.int64) + 1
    if S.size == 0:
        return np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    A = np.flatnonzero(avail).astype(np.int64) + 1
    nA = max(A.size, 1)

    Smask = np.zeros(n + 2, dtype=bool)
    Smask[1:n + 1] = chosen[:n]
    Amask = np.zeros(n + 2, dtype=bool)
    Amask[1:n + 1] = avail[:n]
    target = Amask | Smask

    # Hub score for each addable w: number of partners u in A forming a solution with third slot in A|S.
    # Loop only over the 6 role patterns, each fully vectorised over the (nA x nA) grid.
    w = A[:, None].astype(np.int64)
    u = A[None, :].astype(np.int64)
    hubA = np.zeros(nA, dtype=float)

    # Patterns: (coef_of_w, coef_of_u, denom) solving coef_w*w + coef_u*u = denom*t
    for cw, cu, den in ((a, b, c), (b, a, c)):
        num = cw * w + cu * u
        ok = (num % den == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // den, -1)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != w) & (t != u)
        tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
        hubA += (valid & target[tc]).sum(axis=1)

    # Patterns where the candidate-side appears as the z term: c*w - cw*u = cu*t
    for cw, cu in ((a, b), (b, a)):
        num = c * w - cw * u
        ok = (num % cu == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // cu, -1)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != w) & (t != u)
        tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
        hubA += (valid & target[tc]).sum(axis=1)

    hub = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=float)
    hub[A] = hubA

    # Which addable numbers each candidate kills: build K as (k, n) boolean via scatter over the (k, |S|) grid.
    v = cand[:, None].astype(np.int64)
    s = S[None, :].astype(np.int64)
    K = np.zeros((k, n + 2), dtype=bool)

    def mark(num, mod):
        ok = (num % mod == 0)
        t = np.where(ok, num // mod, 0)
        valid = ok & (t >= 1) & (t <= n)
        rows, cols = np.nonzero(valid)
        K[rows, t[rows, cols]] = True

    mark(a * v + b * s, c)
    mark(b * v + a * s, c)
    mark(c * v - a * s, b)
    mark(c * v - b * s, a)
    mark(c * s - a * v, b)
    mark(c * s - b * v, a)

    K[np.arange(k), cand] = False
    # Restrict to addable victims
    K &= Amask[None, :]

    hub_full = np.zeros(n + 2, dtype=float)
    hub_full[1:n + 1] = hub[1:n + 1] / (float(nA) + 1.0)

    destroyed = (K.astype(float) * hub_full[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
    raw = K.sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    score = 0.5 * (destroyed / (1.0 + destroyed)) + 0.5 * (raw / nA)
    return np.tanh(score)

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """For each candidate, the number of forced-narrowing consequences one level deeper: count completions where the candidate leaves an addable third slot t that would itself be left with few future partners (low remaining danger), i.e. candidates that 'spend' scarce future flexibility are penalised; normalised by total danger mass."""

    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.size
    S = (np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1).astype(np.int64)
    m = S.size
    if m == 0:
        return np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    av = np.zeros(n + 2, dtype=bool)
    av[1:n + 1] = avail[:n]

    density = m / max(n, 1)
    expected = density * density * n

    A = np.flatnonzero(av[:n]) + 1
    danger = np.zeros(n + 2, dtype=float)
    if A.size > 0:
        w = A[:, None].astype(np.int64)
        s = S[None, :].astype(np.int64)
        cnt_w = np.zeros(A.size, dtype=float)
        for coef_k, coef_o, denom in ((a, b, c), (b, a, c)):
            num = coef_k * w + coef_o * s
            okm = (num % denom == 0)
            t = np.where(okm, num // denom, -1)
            valid = okm & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != w) & (s != w) & (s != t)
            tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
            cnt_w += (valid & av[tc]).sum(axis=1)
        for coef_k, coef_o in ((a, b), (b, a)):
            num = c * w - coef_k * s
            okm = (num % coef_o == 0)
            t = np.where(okm, num // coef_o, -1)
            valid = okm & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != w) & (s != w) & (s != t)
            tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
            cnt_w += (valid & av[tc]).sum(axis=1)
        danger[A] = cnt_w

    # total danger mass, used as normaliser
    danger_mass = float(danger.sum())
    if danger_mass <= 0.0:
        return np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    v = cand[:, None].astype(np.int64)
    Srow = S[None, :].astype(np.int64)

    # score the SQUARE of danger[t] (superlinear: candidates that hit already-dangerous
    # addable slots are disproportionately bad), and also count how many low-danger
    # slots they touch (inverse weight).
    hi = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    lo = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    for coef_k, coef_o, denom in ((a, b, c), (b, a, c)):
        num = coef_k * v + coef_o * Srow
        okm = (num % denom == 0)
        t = np.where(okm, num // denom, -1)
        valid = okm & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != v) & (Srow != v) & (Srow != t)
        tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
        d = np.where(valid & av[tc], danger[tc], 0.0)
        hi += (d * d).sum(axis=1)
        lo += np.where(d > 0, 1.0 / (d + 1.0), 0.0).sum(axis=1)
    for coef_k, coef_o in ((a, b), (b, a)):
        num = c * v - coef_k * Srow
        okm = (num % coef_o == 0)
        t = np.where(okm, num // coef_o, -1)
        valid = okm & (t >= 1) & (t <= n) & (t != v) & (Srow != v) & (Srow != t)
        tc = np.clip(t, 0, n + 1)
        d = np.where(valid & av[tc], danger[tc], 0.0)
        hi += (d * d).sum(axis=1)
        lo += np.where(d > 0, 1.0 / (d + 1.0), 0.0).sum(axis=1)

    lo_n = lo / (1.0 + expected)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Position of each candidate relative to the frontier of S: gap between cand and the largest chosen value, signed and normalised, plus a bonus for being just past the frontier."""
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.float64)
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    if S.size == 0:
        # fall back to plain position
        return np.clip((cand - 1) / float(n - 1), 0.0, 1.0)
    hi = float(S.max())
    lo = float(S.min())
    # signed gap beyond the current top of S, normalised by remaining range
    above = np.clip((cand - hi) / max(n - hi, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0)
    # position below the top, normalised by current span
    below = np.clip((hi - cand) / max(hi, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0)
    # just-past-frontier bonus: narrow band above hi
    band = np.exp(-((cand - hi) / max(0.02 * n, 1.0)) ** 2)
    # combine: prefer candidates modestly above frontier, moderate position overall
    return 0.5 * above - 0.5 * below + 0.5 * band

    avf[1:n + 1] = av[:n].astype(float)
    csum = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(avf[1:n + 1])])
    lo = np.clip(np.arange(n + 2) - W, 1, n)
    hi = np.clip(np.arange(n + 2) + W, 1, n)
    dens = (csum[hi] - csum[lo - 1]) / np.maximum(hi - lo + 1, 1)
    scarce = 1.0 / (dens + 1.0 / nA)  # high when local availability is low

    v = cand[:, None].astype(np.int64)
    s = S[None, :].astype(np.int64)

    # Accumulate per-candidate weighted count of partner w in avail sharing a solution with v and some s in S.
    # For each s and each role, compute the partner w; if w is available, add scarcity weight of w.
    total = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    def add_partner(num, mod):
        ok = (num % mod == 0)
        w = np.where(ok, num // mod, -1)
        valid = ok & (w >= 1) & (w <= n) & (w != v) & (s != w)
        wc = np.clip(w, 0, n + 1)
        weight = np.where(valid & av[wc], scarce[wc], 0.0)
        return weight.sum(axis=1)

    # role: x=v, y=s -> z=w ; x=s, y=v -> z=w
    total += add_partner(a * v + b * s, c)
    total += add_partner(b * v + a * s, c)
    # role: z=s, x=v -> y=w ; z=s, y=v -> x=w
    total += add_partner(c * s - a * v, b)
    total += add_partner(c * s - b * v, a)

    # Normalise: divide by (nA * typical scarcity scale) -> roughly in [0,1]
    scale = nA * (1.0 / (m / max(n, 1) + 1e-9))
    return np.tanh(total / (scale + total))

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Position of the candidate relative to the current frontier of S: signed distance (cand - max(S)) / n, plus a soft penalty when cand sits in the sparse upper region, so that ordering differs from raw position."""
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    S = np.flatnonzero(chosen) + 1
    if S.size == 0:
        # no set yet: mildly prefer mid-range numbers over extremes
        return 1.0 - 2.0 * np.abs((cand - 0.5 * (n + 1)) / max(n, 1))
    hi = int(S.max())
    lo = int(S.min())
    # signed distance beyond the frontier, normalized; negative inside (already covered region)
    beyond = (cand - hi) / float(n)
    # gap pressure: how far the nearest chosen neighbour is (local crowding), tiny when dense
    Ssort = np.sort(S)
    idx = np.clip(np.searchsorted(Ssort, cand), 0, Ssort.size - 1)
    left = Ssort[np.clip(idx - 1, 0, Ssort.size - 1)]
    right = Ssort[idx]
    d_left = np.abs(cand - left)
    d_right = np.abs(cand - right)
    nearest = np.minimum(d_left, d_right).astype(float)
    # sparse local neighbourhood -> larger nearest distance -> prefer (helps keep spread)
    spread = np.tanh(nearest / max(1.0, n / 20.0))
    # combine: prefer pushing beyond frontier but reward local isolation near the top
    score = np.tanh(beyond) + 0.5 * spread * (cand >= hi).astype(float) - 0.5 * spread * (cand < lo).astype(float)
    return np.clip(score, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """Signed composition of a candidate's kills: (share of killed value mass - share of killed count) / (sum + eps)."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    k = cand.shape[0]
    vals = np.arange(1, n + 1, dtype=np.int64)

    A = avail.copy()
    A[cand - 1] = False  # exclude candidates themselves from the pool
    A_vals = vals[A]
    sumA = float(A_vals.sum())
    cntA = float(A_vals.size)

    S_vals = vals[chosen]
    S_set = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=bool)
    S_set[S_vals] = True

    coefs = np.array([a, b, -c], dtype=np.int64)
    perms = [(0, 1, 2), (0, 2, 1), (1, 0, 2), (1, 2, 0), (2, 0, 1), (2, 1, 0)]

    u_all = vals  # 1..n
    killed_mask = np.zeros((k, n), dtype=bool)

    for pv, pu, ps in perms:
        cpv, cpu, cps = coefs[pv], coefs[pu], coefs[ps]
        num = -(cpv * cand[:, None] + cpu * u_all[None, :])  # shape (k, n)
        div_ok = (num % cps) == 0
        s_val = num // cps
        in_range = (s_val >= 1) & (s_val <= n)
        s_idx = np.clip(s_val, 1, n) - 1
        in_S = np.zeros_like(div_ok)
        in_S[in_range] = S_set[s_idx[in_range]]
        u_avail = A[None, :]
        u_ne_v = u_all[None, :] != cand[:, None]
        u_ne_s = u_all[None, :] != s_val
        v_ne_s = cand[:, None] != s_val
        valid = div_ok & in_range & in_S & u_avail & u_ne_v & u_ne_s & v_ne_s
        killed_mask |= valid

    u_vals_f = u_all.astype(np.float64)
    killed_mass = (killed_mask * u_vals_f[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
    killed_cnt = killed_mask.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)

    shW = killed_mass / max(sumA, 1e-9)
    shC = killed_cnt / max(cntA, 1.0)
    out = (shW - shC) / (shW + shC + 1e-6)
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """2*(sum over availables u killed by v of coupling(u)^2)/(sum over availables w of coupling(w)^2 + 1) - 1, coupling = # latent arms of w with S."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    k = cand.shape[0]
    A = np.nonzero(avail)[0] + 1
    if A.size == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    Av = A.astype(np.int64)
    P = Av[:, None]
    Q = Av[None, :]
    diff = P != Q

    # coupling(w): number of t != w such that (w,t) with some s in S satisfies the equation
    # under some slot assignment.  Symmetric in the pair, so count per row.
    def pair_works(P, Q, diff):
        # assignment 1: x=P, y=Q, z=s
        num1 = a * P + b * Q
        ok1 = (num1 % c == 0) & diff
        s1 = np.where(ok1, num1 // c, 0)
        v1 = ok1 & (s1 >= 1) & (s1 <= n)
        if v1.any():
            v1 &= chosen[np.clip(s1 - 1, 0, n - 1)]
        # assignment 2: x=P, z=Q, y=s
        num2 = c * Q - a * P
        ok2 = (num2 % b == 0) & diff
        s2 = np.where(ok2, num2 // b, 0)
        v2 = ok2 & (s2 >= 1) & (s2 <= n)
        if v2.any():
            v2 &= chosen[np.clip(s2 - 1, 0, n - 1)]
        # assignment 3: y=P, z=Q, x=s
        num3 = c * Q - b * P
        ok3 = (num3 % a == 0) & diff
        s3 = np.where(ok3, num3 // a, 0)
        v3 = ok3 & (s3 >= 1) & (s3 <= n)
        if v3.any():
            v3 &= chosen[np.clip(s3 - 1, 0, n - 1)]
        return v1 | v2 | v3

    works = pair_works(P, Q, diff)
    pair_ok = works | works.T
    coupling = np.zeros(n + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    coupling[Av] = pair_ok.sum(axis=1)

    cw2 = coupling.astype(np.float64) ** 2
    total = cw2.sum() + 1.0

    # For each candidate v: killed availables u != v that share a solution with v and some s in S.
    V = cand.astype(np.int64)[:, None]   # (k,1)
    U = Av[None, :]                      # (1,|A|)
    mask = U != V

    def killed_mask(V, U, mask):
        # assignment 1: x=V, y=U, z=s
        n1 = a * V + b * U
        ok1 = mask & (n1 % c == 0)
        s1 = np.where(ok1, n1 // c, 0)
        v1 = ok1 & (s1 >= 1) & (s1 <= n)
        if v1.any():
            v1 &= chosen[np.clip(s1 - 1, 0, n - 1)]
        # assignment 2: x=V, z=U, y=s
        n2 = c * U - a * V
        ok2 = mask & (n2 % b == 0)
        s2 = np.where(ok2, n2 // b, 0)
        v2 = ok2 & (s2 >= 1) & (s2 <= n)
        if v2.any():
            v2 &= chosen[np.clip(s2 - 1, 0, n - 1)]
        # assignment 3: y=V, z=U, x=s
        n3 = c * U - b * V
        ok3 = mask & (n3 % a == 0)
        s3 = np.where(ok3, n3 // a, 0)
        v3 = ok3 & (s3 >= 1) & (s3 <= n)
        if v3.any():
            v3 &= chosen[np.clip(s3 - 1, 0, n - 1)]
        # assignment 4: x=U, y=V, z=s
        n4 = a * U + b * V
        ok4 = mask & (n4 % c == 0)
        s4 = np.where(ok4, n4 // c, 0)
        v4 = ok4 & (s4 >= 1) & (s4 <= n)
        if v4.any():
            v4 &= chosen[np.clip(s4 - 1, 0, n - 1)]
        # assignment 5: x=U, z=V, y=s
        n5 = c * V - a * U
        ok5 = mask & (n5 % b == 0)
        s5 = np.where(ok5, n5 // b, 0)
        v5 = ok5 & (s5 >= 1) & (s5 <= n)
        if v5.any():
            v5 &= chosen[np.clip(s5 - 1, 0, n - 1)]
        # assignment 6: y=U, z=V, x=s
        n6 = c * V - b * U
        ok6 = mask & (n6 % a == 0)
        s6 = np.where(ok6, n6 // a, 0)
        v6 = ok6 & (s6 >= 1) & (s6 <= n)
        if v6.any():
            v6 &= chosen[np.clip(s6 - 1, 0, n - 1)]
        return v1 | v2 | v3 | v4 | v5 | v6

    killed = killed_mask(V, U, mask)          # (k, |A|)
    cw2_A = cw2[Av]                            # (|A|,)
    sums = (killed * cw2_A[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
    return 2.0 * sums / total - 1.0

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """(1-r)/(1+r) with r = deg(v)/(E+1): deg = #avail partners t (six slot assignments) whose forced third value w is an integer in [1,n] and avail, E = 6*kA^2/n; high for leaves, low for hubs."""
    a, b, c = int(coef[0]), int(coef[1]), int(coef[2])
    cand = np.asarray(cand, dtype=np.int64)
    k = cand.shape[0]
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0, dtype=np.float64)

    A = np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1  # sorted avail values in 1..n
    kA = A.shape[0]
    E = 6.0 * kA * kA / float(n)

    v = cand[:, None]          # (k,1)
    t = A[None, :]             # (1,kA)
    valid_t = (t != v)         # t != v

    deg = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)

    def count(w_num, w_den):
        # w = w_num / w_den must be integer, in [1,n], avail, and != v, != t
        num = w_num
        den = w_den
        ok = (num % den) == 0
        w = np.where(ok, num // np.where(den == 0, 1, den), -1)
        inr = ok & (w >= 1) & (w <= n)
        wc = np.clip(w, 1, n)
        av = avail[wc - 1]
        distinct = (w != v) & (w != t)
        good = inr & av & distinct & valid_t
        return good.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)

    # v as z: t as x-slot -> w = (c*v - a*t)/b ; t as y-slot -> w = (c*v - b*t)/a
    deg += count(c * v - a * t, b)
    deg += count(c * v - b * t, a)
    # v as x: t as y-slot -> w = (a*v + b*t)/c ; t as z-slot -> w = (c*t - a*v)/b
    deg += count(a * v + b * t, c)
    deg += count(c * t - a * v, b)
    # v as y: t as x-slot -> w = (a*t + b*v)/c ; t as z-slot -> w = (c*t - b*v)/a
    deg += count(a * t + b * v, c)
    deg += count(c * t - b * v, a)

    r = deg / (E + 1.0)
    r = np.clip(r, 0.0, 50.0)
    return (1.0 - r) / (1.0 + r)

import numpy as np

def feature(cand, chosen, avail, n, coef):
    """1 - 2*|q(v) - tgt| where q is the candidate's quantile among available values and tgt = clip(1 - 3*|S|/n, 0, 1)."""
    k = cand.shape[0]
    kA = int(avail.sum())
    if kA < 2:
        return np.zeros(k)
    avail_vals = np.flatnonzero(avail) + 1  # sorted ascending
    p = float(chosen.sum()) / float(n)
    tgt = min(1.0, max(0.0, 1.0 - 3.0 * p))
    # number of available values strictly less than v
    less = np.searchsorted(avail_vals, cand, side='left')
    q = less.astype(np.float64) / float(max(kA - 1, 1))
    return 1.0 - 2.0 * np.abs(q - tgt)

nodes.title: scarcity-weighted future threat
nodes.description: Weight each solution a candidate would create by the reciprocal of how many extensions its partner numbers still have, vectorised.

nodes.title: capacity/reachability of a candidate
nodes.description: Using only (a,b,c,n), count how many offsets t can complete v as a mean (v-b*t, v+a*t) or as a source (v±c*t with v±b*t): a U-shaped 'exposure' of the value itself, involving no state.

nodes.title: local isolation of a candidate
nodes.description: Score candidates by the empty space around them (distance to nearest chosen number, chosen mass in the coefficient-scaled band), preferring values with no possible partners nearby.

nodes.title: decayed exact-offset resonance
nodes.description: Two columns counting chosen numbers at v±a*t, v±b*t, v±c*t with 1/t decay, split left/right to capture the a!=b asymmetry.

nodes.title: wide find: partner_band_density_excess
nodes.description: Density of S within the 'reachable band' of each candidate: how crowded the interval around v (scaled to partners via a,b,c) is, relative to overall density.

nodes.title: role asymmetry (a vs b)
nodes.description: Score candidates by the imbalance between how often they complete equations as the a*x source vs the b*y source, exploiting a!=b in skew/pentad.

nodes.title: endgame preservation
nodes.description: Prefer candidates that leave the largest total number of still-addable numbers (global lookahead of remaining capacity), not just local kills.

nodes.title: coefficient-ratio resonance
nodes.description: Score candidates by alignment with the ratio c/a and c/b: whether v sits at integer multiples of the coefficient ratios from chosen numbers.

nodes.title: position quantile gating
nodes.description: Score candidates by which quantile of the remaining available numbers they sit in, so the preference adapts as the build progresses.

nodes.title: kill-mass asymmetry vs create-mass
nodes.description: Signed difference between how many live numbers a candidate kills and how many new solutions it creates, both normalised by their state-free expectation.

nodes.title: wide find: mean_avail_distance
nodes.description: For each candidate v: how much of the addable range remains reachable as a partner after v is added, measured as the fraction of avail numbers in the 'shadow' interval [c*v/b - something] — approxima…

nodes.title: wide find: local_avail_density_window
nodes.description: For each candidate v, the fraction of its own arithmetic neighbours (v±d, d small) that are still available — measures whether v sits in a dense still-addable cluster or an isolated island.

nodes.title: position gated by remaining capacity
nodes.description: Score candidates by position quantile among remaining available numbers, so the low-number preference adapts as the build progresses and capacity shrinks.

nodes.title: kill vs create mass asymmetry
nodes.description: Signed difference between live numbers a candidate kills and new solutions it creates, both normalised, capturing net damage.

nodes.title: wide find: near_miss_resonance_density
nodes.description: For each candidate, the median over chosen s of the fractional slack of the nearest solvable third value, aggregated as density of close-but-not-exact resonances (a continuous 'near miss' pressure).

nodes.title: parity and gcd class of candidate
nodes.description: Score candidates by residue class mod 2 and gcd(v, c) structure, since a+b=c forces parity relations among x,y,z that differ sharply when a!=b (skew).

nodes.title: two-step survival lookahead
nodes.description: For each candidate, estimate how many available numbers remain addable after v AND after the best follow-up, a cheap two-ply count rather than one-ply kill mass.

nodes.title: coefficient-asymmetry gate
nodes.description: A feature that switches on only when a!=b: measure whether v is more useful as the a-source or b-source, scaled by |a-b|/c.

nodes.title: incoming threat (urgency of a candidate)
nodes.description: For each candidate v count the still-available numbers w that, if added, would block v (w as any role with a witness in S), so fragile-but-good numbers are taken before they are lost.

nodes.title: residue-class balance of S modulo c
nodes.description: Reward candidates whose class mod c is underrepresented among chosen numbers (and that have few mod-c-congruent partners), so S spreads over the c classes where x=y mod c is the only way an equation can complete.

nodes.title: expendable-only kill cost
nodes.description: Weight each available number killed by a candidate by that number's own kill count, so the policy prefers losing numbers that are themselves expensive to keep.

nodes.title: wide find: upper_half_block_frac
nodes.description: Share of still-available numbers whose add would be blocked by candidate together with some s in S, measured only over the upper half of the range (cand>n/2).

nodes.title: frontier ceiling preservation
nodes.description: Score candidates by whether adding v keeps the largest still-addable number high (does not strand the top of the range), normalised by n.

nodes.title: hub vs leaf degree
nodes.description: Count how many potential equation triples (with any two partners in S or avail) v participates in across all roles; prefer low-degree leaves over hubs.

nodes.title: endgame capacity retention
nodes.description: For each candidate, fraction of currently-available numbers that remain addable after v (one-step survival), vectorised via boolean matrix ops.

nodes.title: kill-mass vs live-pool ratio
nodes.description: Ratio of kill mass to remaining live pool, normalised, so a candidate is judged by how much of the surviving pool it removes relative to what is left.

nodes.title: two-level threat lookahead
nodes.description: Solutions a candidate creates weighted by the threat level of its partners one level deeper, capturing cascading danger.
